page: Amazon Web Services m7a.32xlarge is a high-capacity general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system is built on dedicated x86_64 AMD EPYC 9R14 processors operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. It delivers 128 physical cores across 128 vCPUs with a single thread per core configuration, backed by 32 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Architectural support includes AVX-512 vector extensions with VNNI and BF16 support, as well as hardware-accelerated AES and SHA cryptography instructions.

Memory capacity is configured with 512.0 GB of high-frequency 5 GHz DDR5 memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance provides a baseline network throughput of 50 Gbps. Notably, the hardware configuration includes no bundled local storage and zero discrete GPUs, which necessitates network-attached block storage for persistent operational data and virtual disk images.

Benchmark results place the instance in the top decile for multi-threaded compute, registering 384,433.72 in stress-ng multi-core testing and a PassMark CPU score of 126,251.71. Large-block memory tests demonstrate strong memory channel saturation, achieving 550.79 GB/s in read bandwidth and 308.45 GB/s in write bandwidth. Key workload metrics highlight high throughput for in-memory processing, with Redis SET benchmarks achieving 251.75 million operations per second, alongside top-tier execution in Clang software compilation and CPU-driven small model prompt evaluation.

Because the server lacks local NVMe arrays, it prioritizes resource balance over localized I/O latency. The extensive core count and high DDR5 bandwidth provide excellent efficiency for scale-up CPU applications without requiring GPU accelerators. The instance is suited for enterprise application servers, distributed in-memory databases, continuous integration build farms, and heavy microservice architectures.
description: Amazon Web Services m7a.32xlarge is an x86_64 general purpose server powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9R14 processors operating at 3.7 GHz across 128 cores and 128 vCPUs. The instance supplies 512.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 5 GHz alongside a 50 Gbps baseline network interface. It features zero discrete GPUs and no bundled local storage, relying on external network-attached storage for system operations. Benchmark testing demonstrates top-tier multi-core execution in stress-ng and PassMark CPU metrics, paired with uncached read memory bandwidth exceeding 550 GB/s. High-throughput performance is also documented in Redis caching operations and parallel software compilation with Clang. With a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio, the m7a.32xlarge is suitable for multi-threaded continuous integration pipelines, large-scale Redis deployments, enterprise microservices, and general high-concurrency backend compute.
